question: Can explicit process-ownership wording recover the frozen multiprocessing chunk-and-sum byte-histogram endpoint reliably enough for a controlled non-sorting midpoint experiment?

design.strengthening_rule: Name multiprocessing.Pool.map, disjoint chunks, private worker histograms, and parent-side elementwise summation; explicitly exclude multiprocessing.Array, shared memory, and worker writes to shared state.

control_gates.reproduction: Every original-B output must canonically equal the corresponding committed Experiment 009 output.
control_gates.prompt_alignment: The complete strengthened A and B sequences must contain exactly 153 tokens each and require no padding.
control_gates.A_endpoint: All three outputs must retain NumPy, frombuffer, and bincount.
control_gates.B_endpoint: All three outputs must retain multiprocessing or Pool.map, chunks, private or partial histograms, and parent-side summation without proposing a shared-memory update strategy.

interpretation.both_endpoints_pass: Use these exact prompts in a separately frozen non-sorting midpoint and direct-prompt comparison.
interpretation.B_endpoint_fails: The model cannot reliably preserve the intended multiprocessing technique under this interface; report the workload as blocked and do not interpret a midpoint.
interpretation.reproduction_fails: Stop because the model path or environment no longer reproduces Experiment 009.

limitations: This diagnoses endpoint controllability and does not test composition.
The prompt is more explicit than the original and may reduce output diversity.
Automated lexical gates will be checked against the raw text during assessment.
